AccountConsentResponse.description: When the customer accepted a version of the terms and privacy policy, and where.

ActorType.description: Who performed a change, recorded in history and audit (PLAN.md §7.7).

AssistantTicketResponse.description: What n8n may tell the customer. No internal ids.

BookingAddressRequest.description:
Latitude/longitude come from the customer's device ("Detect my location"), if shared. Line1 (house
or flat number) is optional on the website: the technician has the pin and calls the customer.

BookingExtras.description:
Optional details that help the technician: how to get in, who will be there (when it isn't
the person booking), and what the appliance is.

ChannelStatusResponse.description: Whether a channel really delivers (Live) or only writes to the log.

CustomerEstimateResponse.description: The estimate on the tracking page, and whether approving needs a code.

CustomerSessionUser.description: Who is signed in on the customer site. Role is always "CUSTOMER".

IdResponse.description: Response for commands that create or update something addressable.

IntegrationBookingResponse.description:
What the assistant may tell the customer. bool IntegrationBookingResponse.AppointmentConfirmed is always false at
creation: the office agrees the visit time with the customer later (on WhatsApp or a call).

InvoiceLineSummary.description: Type is VISIT | LABOUR | PART | OTHER.

InvoiceSummary.description: CanPayOnline: a payment gateway is set up and something is still due.

LiveLocationResponse.description:
Where the technician is while on the way, and roughly how long until they arrive. Only while
EN_ROUTE and only from a recent report; the customer's own pin is never included, because
tracking links can be forwarded.

LocatedServiceabilityResponse.description:
Located: a provider answered. Pincode is what it found (null if nothing trustworthy); serviceability
is then checked exactly as for a typed PIN code.

MyBookingDetailResponse.description:
One booking inside "My bookings": the same live view as the tracking page, plus what the
customer can do with it. Tracking is null once the job's tracking link has expired.

MyBookingResponse.description: One booking as the customer sees it in "My bookings". The tracking page has the full detail.

MyInvoiceResponse.description: A bill in the customer's own account ("My bills").

NotificationChannelsResponse.description: Channel status, plus which channel one-time codes try first.

OnlineBookingResponse.description:
Session is set when this booking signed the customer in (their phone was just verified);
it is null when they were already signed in.

PublicPriceResponse.description: A typical price a customer may see: what it is, and the range we usually charge.

RequestChannel.description: Where a request came from (PLAN.md §7.6 `leads.source`, Phase 1 subset).

ReviewResponse.description: The customer's rating of the job.

ServiceRequestCard.description: Compact job representation for lists, boards and the technician's day.

TicketPhotoResponse.description: A photo on a support request, as staff see it.

TrackingResponse.description:
What the customer sees at /t/{token} (UX-ARCHITECTURE.md §7): what's happening, who, what it costs,
what's next. Deliberately minimal personal data: first name, locality, no full address.

VisitDetailsView.description: Access notes, the person at home (when not the booker) and the warranty answer.

WarrantyCardResponse.description: The warranty card the customer sees for one job.
